Subject: Regional onboarding runbook + subprocessor attestation request

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Procurement and our DPO have a couple of parallel asks as we get ready for pilot:

1) A concise execution runbook that lists operational checkpoints (what you need from us, what you will configure, timelines) for EU-only onboarding.
2) A current list of Redwood subprocessors that will access customer telemetry/logs and embeddings for EU-resident customers, and any subprocessor attestation templates we should sign.
3) Confirmation of whether logs/cache/kv-store will remain pinned to EU for the production tenancy and what the transient failover window looks like (duration and notification policy).

Could you share a draft runbook and a checklist of acceptance criteria we can feed to legal? We need to sync on evidence items for our audit (SOC2 + DPA addendum). Ideally we'd have something to review by EOD Tuesday to keep our procurement timeline.

Thanks,

Elena Ruiz
DPO, Zenventory Inc.
D: +44 20 5555 0123

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a first-pass execution runbook (redwood-regional-onboard-runbook.xlsx) that lays out checkpoints, owners, and an initial timeline for EU pinning. High level:
- We can commit to EU-residency for request processing, embeddings storage, and operational logs for the production tenancy.
- We propose a 72-hour transient failover window for short-term emergency routing (telemetry replication only) with proactive notice to your DPO and a post-event report.

Next steps I propose:
1) We drop a short checklist in the runbook you can forward to legal.
2) Can we book a 30-min operational sync Tue 10:00 AM CET / 01:00 AM PDT to walk the checklist and evidence items?
3) Please attach your completed subprocessor sheet when you reply — we will map it to our internal roster and call out where we need vendor-level attestations.

I've cc'd Marissa for legal-touch and Karthik for ops feasibility.

Best,

Monica Patel

Saw Monica's draft — quick legal ops notes from our side:
- We'll prepare a DPA addendum that includes an explicit EU data pin for processing and storage, with the transient failover carveout language (72 hours) and mandatory notification/incident reporting.
- Please confirm whether Zenventory requires split-KMS or escrowed keys for EU-only custody — that changes the workstream and timeline.
- We'll require completed subprocessor attestation forms for any 3p vendors that will receive embeddings or identifiable telemetry (even for short-lived caching).

I've dropped a working deck in the shared drive (link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-runbook) with the suggested addendum wording highlighted. Elena — if you can paste the names of critical vendors in reply, we'll call out which need attestations.

All — quick ops confirmation from my side: we can support EU pinning for production tenancy and retain logs in-region. A couple of implementation caveats:
- Telemetry aggregation used for internal quality monitoring will be pseudonymized before any cross-region analytics job. If Zenventory requires raw telemetry export to a non-EU vendor we need that explicitly documented in the addendum.
- Escrowed KMS is operationally feasible but will add ~3 weeks to the kickoff (procurement + HSM provisioning).

Marissa — suggested minor wording for the addendum: add a clause that requires Redwood to notify Zenventory 24 hours prior to any planned transient failover test; incident-driven failover still follows the 72h maximum but must be followed by a report within 48 hours.

Irene Choi
Product Security
Redwood Inference
